description: Bare twin-tube fluorescent batten fitting with an exposed steel reflector

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Bare twin-tube fluorescent batten fitting with an exposed steel reflector Materials: dusty white enamel, insect debris inside, yellowed tubes.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Final measured cost against all four ceilings. Measured bbox 1.25 x 0.1 x 0.115 m. Cost: 368 triangles / 4000, 2 draw calls / 4, 2 materials / 3, 2 unique geometries / 6, 1 textures. Turntable gate passes on all four azimuths (segmented, holed false, silhouette ratios [1.0, 0.557, 1.0, 0.557], interior hole fractions [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]).  Two components at 2 draw calls, 2 materials and 2 geometries against a large ceiling of 4/3/6, and 368 triangles of 4000 -- the prop is plates and cylinders.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 1.250 x 0.100 x 0.115 m against the declared 1.25 x 0.1 x 0.12 -- exact on length and height, 4% under on depth. The conduit stem sits INSIDE the 0.1 m band and reaches the top-center pivot at y 0 rather than standing above it, which is what a top-center pivot requires. The plate is a close-up of a SHORT two-tube fitting, so as everywhere in this kit the form comes from the plate and the proportion from the declaration.

TWO yellowed tubes lying in the channel, seated in a lampholder cup let into each end plate. The previous build was a closed box with no tubes at all. VERIFIED FROM BELOW rather than asserted: the turntable's 20-degree elevation looks slightly DOWN at a fitting that opens downward, so no turntable frame can show them -- a capture at --elevation -35 does, and there the pair of yellowed tubes in an open channel reads exactly as the plate's. That the identity feature is invisible at the review elevation is why this is 0.92 and not higher.

The channel is THREE PLATES -- a top and two sides -- leaving the underside open, with the inner faces a shade darker than the outer and a flat plate closing each end. A solid box is what the previous build shipped and it hid everything. Enamel #d0d2ce at luma 208 and tubes at 204, both far above gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window, so neither needed the tone correction this kit's darker props needed. Grime and rust ride on a post-construction canvas tile.

name: Fluorescent Batten Light
notes: BUDGET CLASS RAISED medium -> large (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.
